blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: The regulation of emerging technologies is often conceived as a strategy of catching up, because legislators arrive too late. Yet gathering signals, constructing scenarios and adapting rules to an anticipated future are fundamental tasks for those entrusted with governance, including the governance of rules themselves. The literature on so-called future law has already shown that anticipation means building institutional capabilities rather than predicting outcomes precisely (anticipatory governance). Taking this premise as its starting point, this article proposes to understand regulation as an exploration of the transformations that may occur. The Ruliological Framework for Anticipatory Regulation distinguishes rules, transformations and trajectories, assessing alternatives and possible developments. Within this approach, computational irreducibility is adopted conditionally, not as a demonstrated property of legal systems. The Quantum Europe Strategy provides a case study and further grounds for reflection.
blocks.zh: 对新兴技术的监管常常被认为是一种赶超策略,因为立法者来得太晚. 然而,收集信号、构建设想情景并调整规则使之适应预期的未来,是那些负责治理的人的基本任务,包括规则本身的治理。 关于所谓未来法律的文献已经表明,预期意味着建立机构能力,而不是精确预测结果(预期治理)。 本条以这一前提为出发点,提议将监管理解为对可能发生的转变的探索. 《预测性管理框架》区分了规则、转变和轨迹,评估了替代办法和可能的发展。 在这种方法中,计算不可减少性是有条件的,而不是作为证明的法律制度财产。 《量子欧洲战略》提供了案例研究和进一步思考的理由。
